title: fix: keep Claude CLI turns working with native questions
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every Claude CLI turn fails when Claude Code advertises its default native `AskUserQuestion` tool.

Related: #174740.

## User Impact

Claude CLI conversations can complete normally without disabling native questions. No configuration changes or migrations are required. Published OpenClaw 2026.10.4 is unaffected by this regression: its default-native flow passes with Claude Code 2.1.300.

## Why This Change Was Made

`extensions/anthropic/cli-backend.ts` intentionally projects `AskUserQuestion` to `ask_user` so the native question follows OpenClaw's mediated question policy. That mapping was introduced in #174740. `ask_user` is already a canonical core tool, but `src/agents/tools/cron-tool-creator-cap.ts:35-44` omitted it from the closed native capability vocabulary. Capturing the native tool surface consequently threw before the model could reply, even when no automation was requested.

Accept `ask_user` at the existing core capture owner. Keep the Anthropic projection, exact-name validation, and rejection of raw `AskUserQuestion` unchanged. The existing scheduled-runtime question restrictions remain in force. Codex's native question bridge does not project its raw `request_user_input` name into this capability list and needs no change.

The production fix adds one vocabulary entry; the owner regression adds a native question capture case and keeps raw harness names rejected. Documentation identifies the canonical capability. No new abstraction, state, schema, protocol, dependency, or configuration key.

## Evidence

Real Claude Code **2.1.300**, isolated Gateway state, loopback-only synthetic Messages endpoint, no real provider credentials. The same retained chat.send → agent.wait harness, native tool settings, turn sequence, and per-turn health checks are used before and after; only checkout identity and evidence labels change.

| Cell | Before: `25933024a1e197fa1a503e84b573a47203fc674f` | After: `60740eb61b81eb529cee4d2c170dadec4f1990bc` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default native tools, including AskUserQuestion | 5/5 turns fail with non-canonical `ask_user` | Two independent runs, each 9/9 status=ok with visible `TRI138010_OK`; initial and per-turn health pass |
| Deny only AskUserQuestion relative to native cell | 9/9 pass | 9/9 status=ok with visible `TRI138010_OK`; initial and per-turn health pass |

Early candidate launches failed initial health before any model turn during shared-host saturation. After the host quieted, a readiness-only probe and both remaining acceptance cells passed. No timeout or assertion was changed.

Current PR head `95bb0f90d37f02f4c604957778e49394b65c14b6` includes only the fix above plus merges from main through `4513e9e09633a740f58b4ccf8802597968868c47`. The cron capture implementation, its regression test, the Anthropic native projection, and this documentation change are unchanged from the E2E-proven commit (empty targeted diff).

Published **2026.10.4** (`OpenClaw 2026.10.4 (383c124)` from npm): 9/9 default-native turns pass, with `AskUserQuestion` confirmed in native initialization and health after each turn. This is a post-release main regression, not a 2026.10.4 backport.

- Owner regression fails before with the reported `ask_user` error; all **18 tests pass** after. Vitest duration 1.79s; wrapper 4.92s.
- Changed-file oxfmt, TypeScript oxlint, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Candidate production build passes; declaration generation was skipped for runtime proof.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38995082420) is green. [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174951#issuecomment-6228672363) reports `ready` on `95bb0f90d37f02f4c604957778e49394b65c14b6`, with no findings. Earlier CI hit an inherited main `mock-exports` failure; main repair #174947 is included.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous vocabulary check without a migration. Blast radius is native capability capture for CLI-backed turns; an incorrect entry could affect captured automation tool restrictions. Raw native tool names remain rejected and this change does not make question tools available to scheduled sessions that otherwise disallow them.
